title: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH
request: The installer currently completes while the launcher directory never reaches PATH in a freshly opened terminal. It picks the profile file from $SHELL alone: on macOS a bash login shell never reads ~/.bashrc, and under `curl … | sh` $SHELL can be empty, sending the block to ~/.profile while the terminal reads ~/.zshrc. It also never checks that its own change took effect. This change makes the installer detect the real login shell, write the block into a profile file a new terminal actually reads, start a clean login shell afterwards and verify that `forgel-code` resolves, and fail with a message naming the edited file and the observed PATH when it does not. --uninstall removes the block from every profile file the installer can have written.

audit.summary: the audit could not run: model call exceeded the 300s deadline

findings.issue: --uninstall no longer honors FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE. The old code removed the block from the overridden profile; the new loop only visits PROFILE_NAMES, so a custom profile edited by a successful or failed install keeps the marked PATH block after uninstall.
findings.suggestion: Add ${FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE:-} to the uninstall candidate set when it is set (deduplicate against PROFILE_NAMES), and add a test that installs and uninstalls with a custom profile path.

findings.issue: --uninstall omits ~/.bashrc, although the previous installer wrote the marked block there for bash when ~/.bashrc existed or when no ~/.bash_profile existed. Upgrading and uninstalling therefore leaves the old PATH block behind.
findings.suggestion: Include ~/.bashrc in the legacy cleanup set for uninstall, update the README list, and extend CANDIDATE_PROFILES/test_uninstall_clears_every_candidate_profile to cover it.
